Hey guys

I know a few of you have been waiting for this and, although I'm not finished assembling, I wanted to get this posted while Z still had his Thunderhawk promotion on.

TL:DR version Certainly worth the money, in fact I've just ordered another!

Bad Things: While this model isn't rage inducing like the Storm Eagle or Spartan it is not a simple or quick assembly (even with the official instructions which are crap) if you are not comfortable straightening resin with hot water, cutting, filing, pinning or filling you aren't going to end up with a decent build.

TAKE YOUR TIME AND DRY FIT EVERYTHING CONSTANTLY! This model is very easy to put together badly!

I can't stress this enough, it's a big build and there is a lot of interplay between the parts which can/will throw the fitting of other parts out enough to mess up the build

There were broken parts - other than the big hull sections everything comes in a big bag and there were several breaks, so far these have all been cosmetic (small vents on the hull) or fixable.

There is thinness - Very minor problem, most notably around the landing gear recess.

This is warpage - nothing majorly warped but on a kit this size even a slight warp will throw the overall fit out. Also where some of the sections are large/thick straightening them can be tricky. I ended up with the lower hull in a basting tray on the hob to get deep enough water hot enough to get it pliable (if you do this don't let the resin touch the metal of the tray!)

This is miscasting - again nothing major but you will either need to fill it or live with it. I've not seen a genuine model in the flesh but it's going to be difficult to pass this recast off as genuine with some of the miscasting mine has.....

Which brings me finally onto.....

You probably need to forget about the detailed interior - while the interior on mine is fine, the top hull is not a great fit. It will be fine if glued/filled but will be a problem if you want to keep it removable to see/show the interior. I also don't think it will take a huge amount of abuse.

The issue is about publishers extracting rents from university budgets; it has nothing to do with editorial control. Here are some relevant extracts (http://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0127502):

"In that sense and contrary to any other business, academic journals are an atypical information good, because publishers neither pay the provider of the primary good—authors of scholarly papers—nor for the quality control—peer review."

"The possibility to increase profits in such an extreme fashion lies in the peculiarity of the economics of scholarly publishing. Unlike usual suppliers, authors provide their goods without financial compensation and consumers (i.e. readers) are isolated from the purchase. Because purchase and use are not directly linked, price fluctuations do not influence demand. Academic libraries, contributing 68% to 75% of journal publishing revenues [31], are atypical buyers because their purchases are mainly controlled by budgets. Regardless of their information needs, they have to manage with less as prices increase. Due to the publisher’s oligopoly, libraries are more or less helpless, for in scholarly publishing each product represents a unique value and cannot be replaced."

"...the ease with which these function can be fulfilled—or are no longer necessary—in the electronic world makes one wonder: what do we need publishers for? What is it that they provide that is so essential to the scientific community that we collectively agree to devote an increasingly large proportion of our universities budgets to them? Of course, most journals rely on publishers’ systems to handle and review the manuscripts; however, while these systems facilitate the process, it is the researchers as part of the scientific community who perform peer review. Hence, this essential step of quality control is not a value added by the publishers but by the scientific community itself."

This is an important issue that deserves media attention, but instead we get exaggerated horse shit like:

"Much of the independence that was once cherished within the scientific community, in other words, has gone by the wayside as these major publishers have taken control and now dictate what types of content get published."
